 Ryan Walker 
 MIL 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Brewers acquired RHP Ryan Walker from the Giants for RHP Blake Holub and RHP Gavin Perry.
 The 2026 version of Walker didn’t seem much like someone worth rostering all winter, but the Brewers obviously think they can get him turned around. Walker was a revelation for the Giants in 2024, posting a 1.91 ERA with a 99/18 K/BB in 80 innings. Since then, he finished with a 4.11 ERA in 61 innings in 2025 and a 7.16 ERA in 33 innings last season. His strikeout rate went from 32 percent in 2024 to 23 percent in 2025 to 15 percent in 2026. He shouldn’t be due more than $1.5 million next year and he’ll be under control through 2029, so a return to form would benefit the Brewers for more than just one season.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Giants optioned RHP Ryan Walker to Triple-A Sacramento. 
 Walker heads back to the minors to open a spot in San Francisco’s bullpen for waiver claim Joel Kuhnel. The 30-year-old former high-leverage reliever is arbitration-eligible for the first time this offseason and could wind up being a non-tender candidate.

 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Giants recalled RHP Ryan Walker from Triple-A Sacramento. 
 Walker gets another shot with San Francisco after struggling in his previous go-around. The 30-year-old former closer is likely ticketed for middle relief work for now. He’s struggled to a bloated 7.52 ERA across 26 1/3 innings of work at the highest level this season. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Giants optioned RHP Ryan Walker to Triple-A Sacramento. 
 Walker had allowed 11 earned runs in his last six appearances while walking four and striking out just one. He’s far removed from the closer role in San Francisco and can be dropped in any leagues where you were holding out for a rebound. 
 Caleb Kilian 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #44 
 Giants manager Tony Vitello told reporters Friday that Caleb Kilian will be their primary closer. 
 Vitello told reporters that Kilian will serve as their closer with Ryan Walker occupying a fireman role in the late innings following his return from a brief minor-league demotion where he made several mechanical adjustments. Kilian has converted four of five save opportunities this season. He’s at least worthy of a speculative roster spot in deeper mixed leagues where every save matters. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Giants recalled RHP Ryan Walker from Triple-A Sacramento. 
 Walker had a 1.93 ERA in 9 1/3 innings in Sacramento, striking out seven and allowing no homers. He’s obviously not being handed the closer’s role back right away, but nobody else in San Francisco has really seized it either. Walker’s ultimately a monitor at this point in most leagues. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Ryan Walker threw 1 2/3 scoreless innings for Triple-A Sacramento on Tuesday, striking out three. 
 In 6 1/3 innings since being demoted to Triple-A, Walker has allowed one run on five hits while striking out seven and walking two. In the meantime, nobody has really distinguished themselves in the Giants’ bullpen. He certainly has a chance to pitch himself back into the closer’s role at some point this season. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Giants optioned RHP Ryan Walker to Triple-A Sacramento. 
 How the mighty have fallen. The 30-year-old right-hander opened the season as the Giants’ closer, but he has registered a miserable 6.46 ERA, 1.89 WHIP and a 14/10 K/BB ratio over 15 1/3 innings in his first 16 appearances. He’ll try to work through his issues at the Triple-A level for the time being. Even in the deepest of leagues, it’s safe for fantasy managers to cut bait here. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Ryan Walker gave up two runs while getting two outs against the Pirates on Saturday. 
 Walker allowed three hits and walked one after coming on during the fifth inning. Those who picked up Caleb Killian or Keaton Winn still aren’t assured much of anything, but that Walker was used so early and fared poorly tonight bodes well for the Giants’ alternatives in the ninth. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 After coming in with the Giants down by two in the eighth, Ryan Walker gave up two runs in his inning against the Padres on Wednesday. 
 Xander Bogaerts hit a two-run homer off him. It’s the fourth straight appearance in which Walker has been scored upon, and his hold on the closer’s role in San Francisco is probably completely gone at this point. That’s good news for Caleb Kilian and Keaton Winn, but with the situation still unsettled and Erik Miller rejoining the mix pretty soon, it’s a tough situation to speculate on in shallow leagues. Kilian might be the best bet. Winn, for what it’s worth, retired two of the three batters he faced after coming into a tie game in the seventh today and was dinged with a run after leaving. 
 Ryan Walker 
 SF 
 Relief Pitcher 
 #74 
 Ryan Walker gave up one run in the eighth inning to take a blown save against the Rays on Sunday. 
 Walker was summoned in the eighth inning with a one-run lead to face the heart of the Rays’ order. He put runners on the corners with no outs on a walk and a single, then blew the lead on a game-tying sacrifice bunt before getting out of the inning. He’d get charged with his second blown save this week as the Giants struggle to find consistency in the late innings. It might be time to start speculating on Keaton Winn and Erik Miller, though it’s unlikely manager Tony Vitello settles on one reliever in the ninth inning.

 Giants acquired RHP Blake Holub and RHP Gavin Perry from the Brewers for RHP Ryan Walker.
 One more spot on the 40-man freed up for the Giants. Holub finished with a 2.10 ERA and a 66/21 K/BB in 55 2/3 innings for the Brewers’ Triple-A affiliate last season. The 28-year-old has never pitched in the majors, but with his mid-90s cutter and a mid-80s slider, he might be decent as a team’s eighth reliever if needed. Perry was the Brewers’ 11th-round pick in the 2026 draft. The Western Kentucky product has yet to debut professionally.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Roldy Brito went 3-for-4 with a homer and a steal for the Gigantes of the Dominican Winter League on Saturday.
 The 19-year-old Brito had the three hardest-hit balls of the game against Licey, coming in at 107, 105 and 104 mph. A very exciting talent in the Rockies system, Brito hit .305/.361/.455 with 10 homers and 41 steals between Low- and High-A last season. He’s a couple of years away, but he could become a regular either in center field or at second base, depending on how the Rockies want to play it.

 Felix Reyes went 2-for-4 with a double Saturday to maintain his .500 average for the Toros of the Dominican Winter League.
 Obviously fully healed from the fractured wrist that ended his season in mid-August, Reyes is 17-for-34 with a homer and six doubles in nine games. The 25-year-old made his MLB debut for the Phillies in April, going 6-for-38 with a homer in 12 games before returning to Triple-A. He ended up batting .287/.318/.511 with 21 homers in 85 games for Lehigh Valley. A free-swinger with limited defensive value, he’s a fringy prospect, but he has power and doesn’t strike out overly much.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Andrés Chaparro went 2-for-4 with a two-run homer and a walk in his season debut for Zulia of the Venezuelan Winter League on Saturday.
 Chaparro has consistently been one of Venezuelan Winter League’s best bats, and he’s back for a fifth year with Zulia despite breaking through with a .263/.360/.525 line in 83 games for the Nationals last season. He should be pretty close to a lock to keep his spot next season, though the Nationals’ offseason moves will determine whether he’s a platoon guy against lefties or if he’s given a chance to be an everyday first baseman.
